```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.align = "center", out.width = "100%")
source("../../_shared/template/viscount_rmd_helpers.R")
library(jsonlite)

read_json_file <- function (arg0_path) {
  txt <- readLines(arg0_path, warn = FALSE, encoding = "UTF-8")
  fromJSON(paste(txt, collapse = "\n"), simplifyVector = FALSE)
}

mod_data <- read_json_file("bolivia_after_independence.json5")
set_data <- read_json_file("bolivia_after_independence_settlements.json")
led_data <- read_json_file("bolivia_after_independence_source_ledger.json5")

clean_text <- function (arg0_s) {
  s <- gsub("&", "and", as.character(arg0_s), fixed = TRUE)
  s <- gsub("_", " ", s, fixed = TRUE)
  s <- gsub("\"", "", s, fixed = TRUE)
  trimws(s)
}

fmt_yr <- function (arg0_y) {
  paste0(round(as.numeric(arg0_y)), "AD")
}

fmt_coord <- function (arg0_coords) {
  lat <- as.numeric(arg0_coords[[1]])
  lon <- as.numeric(arg0_coords[[2]])
  lat_s <- paste0(viscount_fmt_number(abs(lat), 2L), if (lat >= 0) " N" else " S")
  lon_s <- paste0(viscount_fmt_number(abs(lon), 2L), if (lon >= 0) " E" else " W")
  paste0(lat_s, ", ", lon_s)
}

get_val <- function (arg0_pop, arg1_year) {
  y_str <- as.character(arg1_year)
  if (!is.null(arg0_pop[[y_str]])) {
    v <- as.numeric(arg0_pop[[y_str]])
    if (!is.na(v) && is.finite(v)) return(viscount_fmt_pop(v))
  }
  return("-")
}

reg_keys <- names(mod_data$regions)
set_list <- unname(set_data)

# Sort settlements by 2024 population descending
get_p24 <- function (s) {
  if (!is.null(s$population[["2024"]])) as.numeric(s$population[["2024"]]) else 0
}
p24_vec <- vapply(set_list, get_p24, numeric(1))
set_list <- set_list[order(-p24_vec)]

exc_list <- Filter(function (c) identical(c$status, "excluded"), led_data$candidates)
```

# Abstract

This settlement gazetteer compiles geographic coordinates, administrative affiliations and longitudinal population series for 410 catalogued urban settlements, municipal sections and historic cantons across the nine departments of Bolivia from 1825AD to 2026AD.

The dataset integrates the official national censuses of 1846, 1900, 1950, 1976, 1992, 2001, 2012 and 2024, published by José María Dalence and the Instituto Nacional de Estadística (INE), supplemented by historical municipal rolls, colonial-to-republican tributary registers and Andean demographic monographs [@dalence1851bosquejo; @ine1900censo; @ine1950censo; @ine2024censo; @copa2026censosbo; @sanchezalbornoz1978indios; @capriles2023bolivian; @janusek2008ancient; @kirshner2010migration; @andersen2002rural].

The spatial coverage of the gazetteer reflects the historical shifts that transformed republican settlement patterns over two centuries. In the early nineteenth century, sedentary municipal units were confined almost entirely to the high Altiplano and inter-Andean valleys, where silver mining, estate agriculture and indigenous peasant communities sustained traditional administrative capitals such as La Paz, Potosí, Sucre and Cochabamba.

Across the late twentieth and early twenty-first centuries, state-directed colonisation, transport infrastructure and agro-industrial commercialisation produced rapid urbanisation in the eastern lowlands, led by Santa Cruz de la Sierra (2,21M residents in 2024AD), Warnes (151,2k) and La Guardia (147,7k), alongside the metropolitan growth of La Paz-El Alto (2,26M combined basin core) and Cochabamba (974,5k) along the central transport axis.

Every catalogued locality is anchored to precise WGS84 geographic coordinates, assigned to its canonical administrative department and reconciled against 524 candidate records in the project source ledger (410 included municipalities and historic cantons plus 114 documented exclusions).

By subtracting active settlement populations from departmental aggregates, the gazetteer supplies the nucleated component of the Operation Viscount demographic model, preventing artificial concentration in rural raster cells and ensuring an accurate spatial representation of Bolivian settlement history.

# Methodology and Source Ledger Audit

Settlement inclusion in the gazetteer follows three rigorous demographic and archival criteria:
1. **Administrative Autonomy and Census Continuity**: All 343 official Bolivian municipal sections recognized in modern national censuses (2001, 2012 and 2024) are included as autonomous spatial units, supplemented by 67 historical Altiplano cantons, mining camps, valley towns and rubber ports [@copa2026censosbo].
2. **Geographic Coordinate Validation**: All settlement coordinates are verified against Instituto Geográfico Militar (IGM) cartography and GeoNames Bolivia, ensuring that every coordinate pair falls strictly within its respective departmental boundaries.
3. **Reconciliation against Excluded Candidates**: Among the 524 candidates evaluated in the source ledger, 114 records are documented as excluded. These comprise dependent canton hamlets subsumed within larger municipal sections and duplicate toponymic variants within 2 km of canonical centres.

```{r tbl-dept-summary, results='asis'}
sum_rows <- lapply(reg_keys, function (rk) {
  r <- mod_data$regions[[rk]]
  sub_sets <- Filter(function (s) identical(s$region_id, rk) || identical(s$region, rk), set_list)
  n_sets <- length(sub_sets)
  
  get_sum_yr <- function (yr) {
    vals <- vapply(sub_sets, function (s) {
      if (!is.null(s$population[[yr]])) as.numeric(s$population[[yr]]) else 0
    }, numeric(1))
    sum(vals)
  }
  
  p24_vals <- vapply(sub_sets, function (s) {
    if (!is.null(s$population[["2024"]])) as.numeric(s$population[["2024"]]) else 0
  }, numeric(1))
  top_idx <- which.max(p24_vals)
  top_name <- if (n_sets > 0) clean_text(sub_sets[[top_idx]]$name) else "-"
  top_pk <- if (n_sets > 0) p24_vals[top_idx] else 0
  
  data.frame(
    Department = clean_text(r$name),
    Units = as.character(n_sets),
    Sum1850 = viscount_fmt_pop(get_sum_yr("1850")),
    Sum1900 = viscount_fmt_pop(get_sum_yr("1900")),
    Sum1950 = viscount_fmt_pop(get_sum_yr("1950")),
    Sum1980 = viscount_fmt_pop(get_sum_yr("1980")),
    Sum2000 = viscount_fmt_pop(get_sum_yr("2000")),
    Sum2024 = viscount_fmt_pop(get_sum_yr("2024")),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
})
df_sum <- do.call(rbind, sum_rows)

tot_sets <- length(set_list)
get_tot_yr <- function (yr) {
  vals <- vapply(set_list, function (s) {
    if (!is.null(s$population[[yr]])) as.numeric(s$population[[yr]]) else 0
  }, numeric(1))
  sum(vals)
}

df_tot <- data.frame(
  Department = "National Total",
  Units = as.character(tot_sets),
  Sum1850 = viscount_fmt_pop(get_tot_yr("1850")),
  Sum1900 = viscount_fmt_pop(get_tot_yr("1900")),
  Sum1950 = viscount_fmt_pop(get_tot_yr("1950")),
  Sum1980 = viscount_fmt_pop(get_tot_yr("1980")),
  Sum2000 = viscount_fmt_pop(get_tot_yr("2000")),
  Sum2024 = viscount_fmt_pop(get_tot_yr("2024")),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
df_sum <- rbind(df_sum, df_tot)

viscount_table(
  df_sum,
  "Departmental distribution of 410 catalogued settlements and aggregate urban population sums across benchmark years from 1850AD to 2024AD.",
  c("Department", "Settlements", "1850AD Sum", "1900AD Sum", "1950AD Sum", "1980AD Sum", "2000AD Sum", "2024AD Sum"),
  list(label = "tab:dept-summary", font_size = "scriptsize")
)
```

# Departmental Settlement Trajectories

## Department of La Paz

The Department of La Paz encompasses 96 catalogued settlements, representing the most extensive municipal network in Bolivia. Settlement geography is bifurcated between the dense Aymara agricultural cantons of the Lake Titicaca basin and the rapid urbanization of the metropolitan area in the La Paz river canyon and high Altiplano rim [@arbona2008urban].

Table \ref{tab:gaz-lapaz} documents the leading 25 settlements in the department, ordered by 2024 population.

```{r tbl-gaz-lapaz, results='asis'}
sub_lp <- Filter(function (s) identical(s$region_id, "bol_la_paz") || identical(s$region, "bol_la_paz"), set_list)
sub_lp <- head(sub_lp, 25L)

lp_rows <- lapply(sub_lp, function (s) {
  data.frame(
    Municipality = clean_text(s$name),
    Coordinates = fmt_coord(s$coords),
    P1850 = get_val(s$population, "1850"),
    P1900 = get_val(s$population, "1900"),
    P1950 = get_val(s$population, "1950"),
    P1980 = get_val(s$population, "1980"),
    P2000 = get_val(s$population, "2000"),
    P2024 = get_val(s$population, "2024"),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
})
df_lp <- do.call(rbind, lp_rows)

viscount_table(
  df_lp,
  "Leading twenty-five settlements in the Department of La Paz ordered by 2024AD population.",
  c("Municipality", "Coordinates", "1850AD", "1900AD", "1950AD", "1980AD", "2000AD", "2024AD"),
  list(label = "tab:gaz-lapaz", font_size = "scriptsize")
)
```

## Department of Santa Cruz

The Department of Santa Cruz contains 73 catalogued settlements, displaying an extraordinary transition from pre-industrial pastoral isolation to intensive commercial agriculture [@fifer1972bolivia; @schoop1980verstaedterung].

The integrated northern agricultural belt—including Montero, Warnes, Mineros and San Pedro—exhibits sustained population growth driven by mechanized soybean, sugarcane and dairy production.

Table \ref{tab:gaz-santacruz} presents the leading 25 settlements across the department.


## Department of Cochabamba

The Department of Cochabamba contains 55 catalogued settlements, forming the dense demographic heartland of the central valleys [@blanes1984campesinos].

The central valley conurbation connects Cochabamba with Quillacollo, Sacaba, Colcapirhua, Tiquipaya and Vinto, while the tropical Chapare to the northeast encompasses Villa Tunari, Puerto Villarroel, Shinahota and Chimoré.

Table \ref{tab:gaz-cochabamba} presents the leading 20 settlements in Cochabamba.


## Department of Potosí

The Department of Potosí encompasses 42 catalogued settlements, reflecting centuries of mineral extraction across the southern Andes [@platt1982estado; @dunkerley1984rebellion].

Mining centres such as Potosí, Llallagua, Uncía and Uyuni contrast with agricultural valley settlements in Betanzos, Cotagaita and Tupiza.

Table \ref{tab:gaz-potosi} documents the leading 20 settlements in Potosí.


## Department of Oruro

The Department of Oruro contains 35 catalogued settlements across the central Altiplano.

Urban concentration is pronounced around the departmental capital, which acts as the transport junction linking Bolivia with northern Chilean ports, complemented by agricultural and pastoral settlements in Challapata, Caracollo, Toledo and Salinas de Garci Mendoza.

Table \ref{tab:gaz-oruro} records the leading 15 settlements in Oruro.


## Department of El Beni

The Department of El Beni contains 23 catalogued settlements across the Llanos de Moxos.

Urban settlements cluster along navigable river channels and savanna cattle stations, led by Trinidad, Riberalta, Guayaramerín and San Borja [@langer1989economic].

Table \ref{tab:gaz-beni} presents the leading 15 settlements in El Beni.

## Department of Pando

The Department of Pando comprises 16 catalogued settlements across the northern Amazonian rainforest [@zuidema2002demography].

All 16 settlements are documented in Table \ref{tab:gaz-pando}, led by the departmental capital of Cobija on the Brazilian frontier.

## Department of Tarija

The Department of Tarija contains 9 catalogued settlements, all of which are documented in Table \ref{tab:gaz-tarija}.

The departmental capital of Tarija in the Guadalquivir valley contrasts with the rapidly growing Chaco hydrocarbon centres of Yacuiba, Villa Montes, Bermejo and Caraparí [@fifer1972bolivia].
